basis: Congenital skeletal malformations of the thumbs, fingers and toes define the syndrome.
Neoplasm of the hypopharynx; the pharynx belongs to the pulmonary axis.
Malignant CNS tumor arising in the pineal endocrine gland; ocular complications are reported in fewer than 30%.
The definition explicitly requires alcohol-induced organic brain damage, supporting neurologic involvement despite the psychiatric name.
Digestive malignancy umbrella; gastrointestinal sites predominate. Hepatic and pharyngeal locations apply to subsets.
Pulmonary arterial obstruction and resulting lung tissue necrosis define the disease.
Early periodontitis and pretibial plaques define the subtype; joint hypermobility 11/24 and scoliosis 9/27 support musculoskeletal involvement.
Benign blood vessel neoplasm acquired after birth; no specific anatomical site is established.
Focal developmental malformation of the cerebral cortex.
Neoplasm arising in or occupying the external, middle or inner ear.
Chronic inflammatory, T-cell-mediated cutaneous disorder; possible progression to lymphoma is a separate disease risk.
Skeletal dysplasia affecting vertebrae and metaphyses.
Sterol defect; liver fibrosis/cholestasis 30–100%, neurodevelopmental impairment 80–99%, cataracts 2/2; skeletal anomalies omitted by cap.
Congenital myopathy, Moebius facial palsy and Robin oral anomalies define syndrome; ptosis 6/8 supports ocular involvement; pulmonary hypertension 2/8 excluded.
Mesomelic skeletal dysplasia primarily affecting the middle segments of the limbs.
Pontocerebellar hypoplasia with seizures and movement impairment; cerebral visual impairment is neurologic, and dysphagia does not establish gastrointestinal damage.
Isolated congenital ocular motor dysfunction with horizontal jerk nystagmus; no additional CNS disease is established.
Isolated congenital absence or dystrophy of fingernails and toenails.
Hodgkin lymphoma arising in the spleen; splenic origin supports haematologic and lymphoma supports infectious_immune.
Childhood tumor arising from CNS glial or mixed glial-neuronal tissue.
Developmental delay 28/28 and intellectual disability 21/24 define a neurodevelopmental disorder; hearing impairment 5/25 is below threshold.
Bone marrow failure and diabetes define the syndrome; pancytopenia occurs in 3/4 and diabetes in 4/4. Nevi alone do not establish damaging skin disease.
Chronic immune-mediated photosensitivity dermatitis with persistent eczematous skin inflammation.
Immune-mediated inflammatory skin disease producing epidermal atrophy and dermal fibrosis, commonly on genital skin.
Chronic intertwin blood transfusion causes donor anemia and recipient polycythemia; fetal blood involvement gives this obstetric condition an axis.
